keyTerms.definition: The answer keys file for Unit 03 of Stanford CS229S, dated 2026-10-06.
Answers provided in a closed-book format, kept separate from the lesson file.
The Stanford course covering systems for machine learning, offered under the Stanford Frontier AI program.

recall.question: What is the Unit 03 Keys document and when was it dated?
recall.answer: The Unit 03 Keys document is the answer keys file for the U03 lesson. It is dated 2026-10-06.

recall.question: What format do the Unit 03 Keys answers use, and how should they be stored?
recall.answer: The answers are closed-book answers. They should be kept separate from the lesson file.

keyTerms.definition: C = 6PD + 12LnTD: dense term plus the attention term.
12LnTD over D tokens in sequences of length T.

recall.question: Write the full training FLOP formula.
recall.answer: C = 6PD + 12LnTD: dense term plus the attention term over D tokens in sequences of length T.

keyTerms.definition: Dense training FLOPs for P parameters and D tokens.
333312 in the toy: 309504 dense plus 23808 attention.

recall.question: Toy values above. Recompute by hand.

keyTerms.definition: An estimate that used only 6PD, which makes the attention term at T = 16384 large.
A measured term at T = 16384 that is large because the estimate used 6PD only.

recall.question: Why is the attention term at T = 16384 large?
recall.answer: The estimate used 6PD only. Adding 12LnTD lets the profiler count it.

keyTerms.definition: 12T/(72n): about 2 percent at T=512, n=4096.
About 2 percent here.

recall.question: T = 512. Attention share?
recall.answer: T = 512, n = 4096: attention/dense = (12 512)/(72 4096) = 0.021, about 2 percent. Negligible.

keyTerms.definition: The hypothesized quadratic model relating step time to T, including a constant, a linear term, and a squared term.
A model without the quadratic term that underfits the step time versus T data and lacks the T^2 component.

recall.question: When does the quadratic term become significant in the step time versus T fit, and what is requested in the report?
recall.answer: The quadratic term becomes significant past approximately 8K, and a 6PD-only model without T^2 underfits. The report should include both sets of coefficients.

keyTerms.definition: 2P + 4LTn: weights plus cached-key scores.
Part of the per-token 2P + 4LTn FLOPs.

recall.question: Write the per-token decode FLOP formula.
recall.answer: Per token: 2P + 4LTn FLOPs (weights plus cached-key scores).

keyTerms.definition: 2 times 13e9 times 50 = 1.3e12.
Small here.

recall.question: P = 13e9, 50 tokens. Decode FLOPs.
recall.answer: 2 13e9 50 = 1.3e12 FLOPs dense, attention add-on is small. About 1.3e12.

keyTerms.definition: Same FLOPs, different bytes: decode is bandwidth-bound, so bytes set speed.
Fewer bytes moved per token.

recall.question: Two models have the same FLOPs but run at different speeds. Explain.
recall.answer: Same FLOPs but different bytes: one model moves fewer bytes (quantized weights, smaller cache). Decode is bandwidth-bound, so bytes set speed.

keyTerms.definition: Reuses weights 64x, raising intensity toward compute-bound.
Unchanged, and time per token falls.

recall.question: Batch 64. Does 2P per token still hold?
recall.answer: Yes: 2P per token still holds per sequence, batch 64 reuses weights 64x, raising intensity toward compute-bound. FLOPs per token unchanged, time per token falls.

keyTerms.definition: Per-token time correlates with bytes (high R^2), weakly with FLOPs (low R^2).
The bandwidth-bound regime.

recall.question: State the bytes-vs-FLOPs hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: per-token time correlates with bytes (R^2 high) and weakly with FLOPs (R^2 low) at batch 1. Report both R^2.

keyTerms.definition: 2 * B * T * L * n * bytes-per-number.
The factor of 2 in the cache formula.

recall.question: Write the KV byte formula.
recall.answer: KV bytes = 2 * B * T * L * n * bytes-per-number (keys plus values, fp16: x2).

keyTerms.definition: Cache for B=1, T=32768, L=32, n=4096 in fp16.
2^30 bytes.
A cache used during inference that grows with the sequence length T while the model weights stay fixed in size.
A listed fix for KV cache memory pressure that reduces the numerical precision used to store the cache.

recall.question: What problem does the KV cache pose and what fixes does the section list?
recall.answer: The KV cache grows with the sequence length T while the weights stay fixed. The section lists smaller batch, shorter context, paged or blocked cache, or quantization of the cache as fixes.

keyTerms.definition: Grouped-query attention: h_kv = 8 heads here.
Cache shrinks by h_kv/h.

recall.question: GQA with 8 KV heads, 32 query heads. New formula?
recall.answer: KV heads h_kv = 8: cache = 2 B T L (h_kv d) bpe = 2 B T L n (h_kv/h) bpe. Here 1/4 of the MHA cache.

keyTerms.definition: C/T with C from the cache byte budget.
Sets the constant C.

recall.question: State the 1/T hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: max batch B_max(T) = C/T with C from the cache byte budget. Fit B_max vs 1/T, report C and R^2.

keyTerms.definition: The parallel forward pass over the prompt that builds the KV cache.
Token-by-token generation after prefill.

recall.question: Define prefill in one line.
recall.answer: Prefill is the parallel forward pass over the prompt that builds the KV cache before decode starts.

keyTerms.definition: 2PD for the forward pass.

recall.question: P = 7e9, T = 8192. Prefill FLOPs (dense term only).
recall.answer: Dense term: 2 7e9 8192 = 1.15e14 FLOPs.

keyTerms.definition: Naive attention materializes 65536^2 scores per head.
Or chunk the prefill to bound score memory.

recall.question: At T = 65536, what term dominates first-token time?
recall.answer: The T^2 score term: naive attention materializes (65536)^2 scores per head. Tile or chunk the prefill.

keyTerms.definition: 4 chunks: peak score memory is 1/16 of the full matrix.
Chunk size here.

recall.question: Prefill chunked into 4. Peak score memory now?
recall.answer: Chunked into 4: peak score memory per chunk is (16384)^2 per head-set, 1/16 of the full matrix.

keyTerms.definition: Quadratic in T naive, linear tiled.
Where scores exceed fast memory.

recall.question: State the bend-point hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: time-to-first-token is quadratic in T with naive attention and linear with tiled attention, the bend point is where scores exceed fast memory. Report the bend T.

keyTerms.definition: ~T FLOP/byte.
~B FLOP/byte, ~1 at batch 1.

recall.question: Write both intensities.
recall.answer: Prefill intensity ~T FLOP/byte, decode intensity ~B FLOP/byte (batch 1: ~1).

keyTerms.definition: Prefill at T=64: I=64 < 150.
Decode at B=200: I=200 > 150.

recall.question: Toy ridge 150. Classify prefill T = 64 and decode B = 200.
recall.answer: Prefill T=64: I=64 < 150, memory-bound. Decode B=200: I=200 > 150, compute-bound.

keyTerms.definition: A state where compute is the limiting factor rather than bandwidth, so adding more bandwidth does nothing.
A resource that is not the limit when decode is compute-bound, so increasing it provides no benefit at this batch.

recall.question: What should you check when decode is compute-bound at the current batch?
recall.answer: Check the batch against the ridge, because bandwidth is not the limit and more bandwidth changes nothing.

keyTerms.definition: Weights stored as 8-bit integers that halve the byte count while keeping FLOPs fixed.
The compute measure expressed as approximately 2B FLOPs per byte in this configuration.

recall.question: What happens to decode intensity when int8 weights halve the bytes at fixed FLOPs?
recall.answer: Decode intensity doubles to approximately 2B FLOPs per byte because halving bytes at fixed FLOPs doubles the ratio.

keyTerms.definition: Near the ridge point: tokens/s rises linearly then flattens.
Throughput vs batch.

recall.question: State the knee hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: tokens/s rises linearly with batch (bandwidth-bound) then flattens (compute-bound), the knee sits near B = ridge point. Report the knee B.

keyTerms.definition: Trades latency for throughput: one weight read serves B requests.
Tokens per second across the batch.

recall.question: Define the batching tradeoff in one line.
recall.answer: Batching trades latency for throughput: one weight read serves B requests.

keyTerms.definition: 16 requests over 0.035 s.

recall.question: In the toy model, what are the latency and total throughput at batch 16?
recall.answer: Toy model: latency = 0.020 (1+0.05 15) = 0.035 s. Throughput = 16/0.035 = 457 tok/s total.

keyTerms.definition: The state where adding batches adds latency without any throughput gain.
Lowering the batch size until it reaches the knee point, which cuts latency.

recall.question: What should you do when batching is past the compute roof?
recall.answer: Batching adds latency with no throughput gain. The fix is to reduce the batch to the knee.

keyTerms.definition: The bound that gives B-1 <= 5 and max batch 6.

recall.question: SLO caps latency at 25 ms. Max batch in the toy model?
recall.answer: 0.020 (1+0.05 (B-1)) <= 0.025 gives B-1 <= 5, so max batch 6 in the toy model.

keyTerms.definition: Best B: throughput saturates while p99 latency keeps rising.
Tail latency to report with throughput.

recall.question: State the saturation hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: throughput saturates with batch while p99 latency keeps rising, the best B is at the saturation knee. Report both curves.

keyTerms.definition: c is the draft/target per-token time ratio.
Gamma is the number of drafts per round.

recall.question: What does the variable a represent?
recall.answer: The variable a represents the per-token acceptance probability.

keyTerms.definition: Expected accepted tokens: (1-0.8^6)/0.2 = 3.689.

recall.question: C = 0.05, gamma = 5, a = 0.8. E[k] and speedup.

keyTerms.definition: It is the first cause of E33 and you measure it where the formula E[k] collapses.
It is the second cause of E33 and you measure it by comparing draft versus target step time.

recall.question: What are the two causes of E33?
recall.answer: The two causes of E33 are low acceptance a and slow draft c. Low acceptance a is measured where the formula E[k] collapses, and slow draft c is measured by comparing draft vs target step time.

keyTerms.definition: When each round costs one target step.
Always helps until verification slows.

recall.question: What does the speedup formula become when every round costs one target step?
recall.answer: Speedup = E[k]/1 = E[k]: every round costs one target step. Larger gamma always helps until verification slows (C08 slope).

keyTerms.definition: The value of gamma where speedup reaches its highest point, matching the argmax of E[k]/(gamma*c+1).
The speedup that the hypothesis predicts will rise and then fall as gamma changes.

recall.question: What pattern does the E35 hypothesis predict for measured speedup versus gamma, and how is the peak identified?
recall.answer: Speedup rises then falls as gamma changes. The peak gamma matches the argmax of E[k]/(gamma*c+1), and both peaks should be reported.

keyTerms.definition: One parallel forward pass over draft tokens, like a prefill.
Known inputs to the target.

recall.question: Why is verification one step, not gamma?
recall.answer: Draft tokens are known inputs, so the target computes all gamma+1 distributions in one parallel forward pass, like a prefill.

keyTerms.definition: 1 + 0.05*8 for gamma=8.
The cost unit.

recall.question: Gamma = 8, slope 0.05. Verification steps.
recall.answer: 1 + 0.05*8 = 1.4 target steps.

keyTerms.definition: The verification pass becomes compute-heavy when the context is long or gamma is huge.
Gamma is a model parameter used in the formula one plus slope times gamma.

recall.question: What broke when the verification pass became compute-heavy?
recall.answer: The approximately one step model broke. The model is then written as one plus slope times gamma.

keyTerms.definition: Drafts must be re-encoded so verification can run as a prefill over the prompt plus drafts.
Verification becomes a prefill over prompt and drafts, which costs more than one step.

recall.question: Why must drafts be re-encoded for verification?
recall.answer: Verification becomes a prefill over the prompt plus drafts, which costs more than one step. Drafts should be kept in the cache.

keyTerms.definition: The measured duration required for verification, hypothesized to grow linearly with gamma at a small slope.
A parameter whose value influences verification time and whose optimal setting is determined by the fitted slope.

recall.question: What does the E40 hypothesis claim about verification time and gamma, and what should be reported?
recall.answer: The hypothesis states that verification time is linear in gamma with a small slope, and that the slope sets the optimal gamma. The fitted slope should be reported.

keyTerms.definition: Accept x_i with probability min(1, p(x_i)/q(x_i)).
Target over draft probability.

recall.question: Write the accept probability.
recall.answer: Accept x_i with probability min(1, p(x_i)/q(x_i)).

keyTerms.definition: Equals 0.286 in this example.

recall.question: Q = 0.7, p = 0.2. Accept prob.

keyTerms.definition: The distribution used during resampling that the text says should be norm(max(0, p-q)) but may be wrong.
A property the output should have, which the text says fails when the resample distribution is wrong or the bonus token mishandled.

recall.question: What causes the output to fail to be p-distributed in this bug class?
recall.answer: The resample distribution is wrong, not norm(max(0, p-q)), or the bonus token is mishandled.

keyTerms.definition: Then a = 1: every draft accepts.
Full acceptance when draft equals target.

recall.question: Q = p exactly. What is a?
recall.answer: q = p: min(1, p/p) = 1, so a = 1. Every draft accepts.

keyTerms.definition: Over 50K rounds matches p within sampling noise.
The tolerance for the histogram check.

recall.question: State the histogram hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: over 50K rounds the output histogram matches p within sampling noise. Report max bin deviation.

keyTerms.definition: Required for draft and target.
Exact norm(max(0, p-q)) required.

recall.question: Name the two exactness assumptions.
recall.answer: (1) Same tokenizer/vocabulary for draft and target. (2) Exact resample distribution norm(max(0, p-q)).

keyTerms.definition: The value of a in this example.
Equals 1 in this example.

recall.question: Q = p. Acceptance rate?

keyTerms.definition: Different tokenizers mean different distributions over different spaces.
Rejection-sampling is an identity that no longer applies when tokenizers differ.

recall.question: Why do outputs diverge from p in this section?
recall.answer: Different tokenizers create different distributions over different spaces, so the rejection-sampling identity no longer applies. Outputs then diverge from p.

keyTerms.definition: The mass max(0, p-q) that dropping on reject without resampling loses.
Output is not p-distributed.

recall.question: Resample skipped on reject (just drop). Is output still p?
recall.answer: No: dropping on reject without resampling loses the residual mass max(0, p-q). Output is not p.

keyTerms.definition: Output diverges measurably from p (toy only).
Measurably from p.

recall.question: State the tokenizer-swap hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: with mismatched tokenizers the output distribution diverges measurably from p (toy only).

keyTerms.definition: Equals (1 - a^(gamma+1)) / (1 - a).

recall.question: Write the E[k] formula.

keyTerms.definition: The value used in (1 - 0.6^5)/0.4 = 2.306.

recall.question: What is E[k] in the worked example?

keyTerms.definition: Breaks: real acceptance falls with position.
Fit instead of one a.

recall.question: Why might measured speedup fall short of the formula?
recall.answer: The constant-a assumption broke: real acceptance falls with position (later drafts condition on earlier ones). Fit per-position a_i.

keyTerms.definition: Tokens per round: all drafts plus the bonus token.
The extra token per round.

recall.question: A = 1. Tokens per round?
recall.answer: gamma + 1 tokens per round (all drafts plus the bonus token).

keyTerms.definition: Per-position acceptance falls with i.
Report it.

recall.question: State the declining-a_i hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: per-position acceptance a_i declines with i. Report the fitted a_i curve.

keyTerms.definition: E[k] / (gamma*c + 1).
Cost per round in target steps.

recall.question: Write the speedup formula.
recall.answer: Speedup = E[k] / (gamma*c + 1).

keyTerms.definition: E[k]=5.695 over cost 1.7.
Computed as (1-0.9^8)/0.1, with cost 1.7 and speedup 3.35x.

recall.question: A = 0.9, gamma = 7, c = 0.1. Speedup.

keyTerms.definition: Slower than 1 step at long context.
Below the assumed a on this workload.

recall.question: Name two causes when measured speedup falls short of the formula.
recall.answer: Causes: (1) verification slower than 1 step (long context), (2) measured a below the assumed a on this workload.

keyTerms.definition: Up until verification cost (1 + slope*gamma) bends the curve.
The speedup when rounds cost one step.

recall.question: C = 0 (free draft). Best gamma?
recall.answer: Speedup = E[k], push gamma up until verification cost (1 + slope*gamma) bends the curve.

keyTerms.definition: Formula vs measured speedup agree within it.
Over (a, c, gamma).

recall.question: State the error-map hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: formula vs measured speedup agree within 20 percent, deviations trace to the verification slope. Report the error map over (a, c, gamma).
